sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Extrusion and Potting of Hollow Fiber Polyethersulfone Dialyzers

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French-inspired, Napoleonic tradition) with specific SCSp provisions under the Law of 10 August 1915 as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Income Tax Convention (1996) and Amending Protocol (2004)
EU Treaty framework (TFEU) for cross-border medical device trade

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners and its implementing Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019; Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013 creating the SCSp; EU AML Directive 2015/849 as transposed; CSSF Regulation 12-02 where an obliged financial-sector entity is engaged.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: SCSp deed / partnership agreement (contrat de société) reconducing to Luxembourg law
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (notarial deed) or all partners under private deed with legalized signatures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if signed outside Luxembourg) or Luxembourg notarization (if signed in Luxembourg)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing (extract) of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry / company registrar of the general partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by that jurisdiction's competent authority; where not a Hague member, Luxembourg consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney executed by partners in favour of the formation agent or representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or authorized officers of the corporate partner / each natural-person partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, depending on place of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passport and proof of residence of each ultimate beneficial owner and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary, embassy, or AML/CFT obliged entity in the home country of the person
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification and, where required by the Luxembourg filing agent, apostille or consular certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-funds and bank reference letter for initial capital and future settlement under SWIFT_LC / TT_Wire
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank maintaining the partner or UBO account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-certified true copy; if signed by a non-EU bank, apostille or legalization may be requested

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Risk-based AML/CFT CDD is mandatory for the SCSp formation, executed by the Luxembourg notary or registered agent and by the bank. Screening must cover all signatories, partners, managers, and any person owning or controlling 25% or more of the partnership. It includes (i) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database (FISMA), (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) Luxembourg national sanctions list maintained by the Ministry of Finance, and (iv) OFAC SDN List where USD clearing under SWIFT_LC / TT_Wire is anticipated. PEP identification applies the FATF Recommendation 12 definition and is enhanced for foreign politically exposed persons if a senior function was held within 12 months. Negative news, adverse-media and sanctioned-entity checks are recorded in the internal CDD file; denial of clearance blocks incorporation and account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS online portal (https://www.lbr.lu); e-request service for name reservation and RCS filings
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name may be in any language using Latin script. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters with a certified transliteration if needed. The suffix or prefix 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' / 'SCSp' is mandatory and must appear before or after the chosen name. RCS filing forms are processed in French; Luxembourgish and German are also accepted. The name must be distinctive within Luxembourg and must not create confusion with existing RCS-registered names or protected public names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Banca unless authorised under Luxembourg banking law
Insurance / Assurance / Versicherung unless authorised under insurance law
Fiduciary / Fiduciaire / Trust unless the service provider is licensed under AML law
Luxembourg / Lëtzebuerg / État du Luxembourg when the name suggests a state connection without prior ministerial authorisation
European Union / EU / Euro when implying an EU institution or currency authority without authorisation
Sterile / GMP / CE / ISO or similar medical-device quality tokens if the corresponding MDR certification has not yet been obtained
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The LBR name reservation is valid for 90 days and is not automatically renewable. If a cleared name has not been consumed by filing, the applicant must repeat the LBR online reservation request. If the LBR refuses a name, the applicant may deliver an online reconsideration request within 15 calendar days through the LBR e-request platform, explaining why the name is distinguishable and does not conflict with a protected token. If refused upon reconsideration, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Tribunal Administratif of Luxembourg within three months of notification. The applicant is advised to trigger a new name-clearance path in tandem so as not to delay incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Luxembourg's Law of 31 May 1999 permits shared service and domiciliation offices for administrative purposes; an SCSp may use an approved domiciliation agent for its registered seat. However, because the business purpose includes the manufacture of sterile dialysis hemofilters under ISIC_3250, a purely virtual office is not sufficient. The entity must have access to a physical EU/EEA-licensed or equivalently licensed manufacturing site, and the SCSp's commercial substance file must document key operations, storage, quality control and management. Virtual office use is limited to the registered seat and mail service only.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for corporate registry and AML inspections of the SCSp in Luxembourg: approximately 15% in any financial year for a low-risk standard registration. Very high for health-sector compliance: under MDR (EU) 2017/745, the competent authority (Ministère de la Santé / Direction de la Santé) is expected to perform an announced or unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12-18 months of licensed manufacturing, and thereafter plausibly every 2-3 years; unannounced re-inspections exceed 90% probability for sterility-critical products.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS name availability search and name reservation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: LBR statutory tariff; approx. EUR 40 per reservation request

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of SCSp deed and appendices (if notarial form selected)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff; market estimate for a standard SCSp deed, EUR 800

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostilles and consular legalization package for corporate partners and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authorities of each issuing state and/or Luxembourg consulates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Public fee per apostille; approx. USD 25-40 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation into French or German of source-company constitutional documents and UBO identification data
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator admitted before Luxembourg courts / LBR accepted translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per page; typically USD 45-70 per page with notarial certification

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg consolidated Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 101 et seq. (Société en Commandite Spéciale regime inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013); filing regime under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and implementing regulations administered by Luxembourg Business Registers.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), electronic filing portal at www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership agreement (contrat de société) for a société en commandite spéciale, executed either by authentic act before a Luxembourg notary or as a private deed, filed with the RCS together with the statutory data statement for registration and RESA publication.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital applies to an SCSp; the capital is freely fixed in the partnership agreement and may be denominated in any currency. No escrow account or bank certificate of capital deposit is required by Luxembourg law; contributions may be called in installments as contractually agreed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner of [•] SCSp (the 'Partnership') approves and adopts the Partnership Agreement dated [•] governed by the amended Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915; RESOLVED, that the General Partner subscribes to all interest allotments in the Partnership's capital table, and that limited partners' contributions are made against issuance of partnership interests; RESOLVED, that the Partnership's registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg; RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Manager and [Name] is appointed AML Compliance Officer; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Manager is authorized to file the Partnership with the RCS, to publish the statutory notice in RESA, to obtain the business establishment permit, and to open bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability screening and drafting of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg corporate counsel and RCS name pre-screening via Luxembourg Business Registers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the proposed corporate name against RCS records to eliminate conflicts; define the general partner and limited partners, capital allocations, profit-sharing ratios, transfer restrictions, and governance powers of the general partner; select the registered office municipality and finalize the partnership agreement in French, German, or English.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each partner
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
Draft capitalization table and contribution schedule
Certificate of incorporation and statutory extract of corporate general partner, if any
Integrity and professional qualification information for the industrial permit assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS flags a name conflict, counsel re-submits an alternative name or a consent letter from the conflicting entity; objections are curable within 15 days of the RCS notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership deed and AML/KYC file completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg (Luxembourg notary public) or contracting counsel for a private deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the partnership agreement in authentic or private form; collect the statutory data required for RCS filing (identity of managers, capital, registered office); complete anti-money-laundering client due diligence in line with the Law of 12 November 2004, including beneficial ownership declarations.
required_dossiers: Final partnership agreement (acte notarié or sous seing privé)
AML/KYC forms and identification documentation of partners and beneficial owners
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or landlord consent)
List of managers and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A notary may require updated beneficial-ownership evidence before countersigning; any defect is cured by an amending addendum and re-notarization of the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration, issuance of RCS number, and RESA publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers e-filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic registration application through lbr.lu together with the executed deed, the statutory data form, and the filing fee; the RCS verifies legality of the filing and allocates the RCS registration number; the filing data is subsequently published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement in PDF format
RCS electronic application form with statutory data
Identity documents of managers and authorized signatories
Consent of the registered office holder
Proof of filing fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, a corrective statement must be filed within 15 days; unresolved objections may lead to refusal, subject to judicial review before the Tribunal d'arrondissement of Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment permit for industrial activity (autorisation d'établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des classes moyennes (General Directorate for the Middle Classes), application filed on Guichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the establishment permit application after RCS registration; demonstrate professional qualification for managing an industrial operator, absence of disqualifying criminal record, and integrity of the managers; specify the manufacture of dialysis consumables under NACE code 32.50 and the operational address of the production site.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration
Professional qualification certificates or diplomas
Extract of criminal record (bulletin n°3) of managers
Description of the manufacturing plant and product line
Confirmation of employer registration with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale or undertaking to register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon refusal, the applicant may submit an administrative reconsideration request within 3 months and thereafter appeal to the Administrative Tribunal within 3 months of the refusal decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, social security, statistical registration, and bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); STATEC; a Luxembourg credit institution or authorized payment institution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Luxembourg VAT identification number, register the SCSp as an employer with the CCSS, obtain the national business identification number, and open operating and collection bank accounts upon presentation of the RCS extract, establishment permit, and partnership governance documents.
required_dossiers: RCS extract (dated within 3 months)
Business establishment permit
Partnership agreement and proof of registered office
Identity documents of authorized signatories
AML/KYC file of the partnership, including beneficial ownership details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registrations may be cured by voluntary disclosure to the AEDT and CCSS with penalty mitigation in good-faith cases; banks may request a fresh RCS extract, obtainable within one business day from Luxembourg Business Registers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des classes moyennes (business establishment licensing), in coordination with the Ministère de la Santé – Direction de la Santé for medical device manufacturing oversight under Regulation (EU) 2017/745.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement pour industriels (establishment permit for industrialists) together with manufacturing-site conformity registration for hollow-fiber dialysis hemofilters as medical devices under Regulation (EU) 2017/745, evidenced by the applicable Notified Body certificate for Class IIa/IIb devices.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified establishment (établissement classé) under the Law of 9 May 2014 and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 June 2016. The extrusion, potting, and cleaning plant falls under Class 2 requiring an environmental authorization; an EIA screening procedure is triggered under the Law of 15 May 2018 if waste-solvent or VOC throughput exceeds Annex IV threshold volumes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to the municipal sewer must meet municipal bylaws (pH 6-9.5, COD ≤ 1000 mg/L, TSS ≤ 500 mg/L, no priority hazardous substances); air emissions must comply with the solvent-emission BAT-AELs of Directive 2010/75/EU, with waste-gas VOC concentration ≤ 20 mg C/Nm3 after abatement; hazardous waste handling and tracking under the Law of 21 March 2012; cleanroom operations to ISO 14644-1 and quality systems to ISO 13485 for the sterile hemofilter line.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) and the municipal building authority prior to commissioning; structural load and building completion certification by an accredited engineer; workplace compliance inspection by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering machine safety, chemical agent exposure, pressure equipment, and medical product labelling; registration of workers with the Association d'assurance accident (AAA) for occupational accident coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; official portal: MyGuichet.lu (guichet.lu)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident taxable persons must obtain a Luxembourg VAT identification number (numéro de TVA). Application via Form 640/AEDT e-filing on MyGuichet.lu; the SCSp must first obtain a national registration number (matricule) from the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR). A local VAT tax representative may be required for non-EU suppliers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - SCSp is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes (no CIT/MBT/NWT at partnership level); it constitutes a separate taxable person for VAT if it performs taxable economic activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election under Luxembourg law. An SCSp may opt for VAT liability and register as a taxable person; hybrid mismatch treatment is governed by ATAD provisions. Consent is required from the general partner (gérant) and may be specified in the partnership agreement.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No fixed economic turnover threshold for established businesses; any taxable supply triggers compulsory registration. Small enterprises may apply the optional annual turnover franchise of EUR 35,000. Non-residents are subject to the same EUR 35,000 threshold for intra-EU distance sales (cross-border).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate for B2B invoices. E-invoicing is mandatory for B2G (public-sector) invoices since mid-2022; no API clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0%) applies to the export of goods outside the EU provided the exporter dispatches or transports the goods out of the EU or a third party acts on the exporter's behalf. Documentation must prove the physical exit from the EU within the applicable timeframe.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD - Single Administrative Document)
Transport documents: Bill of Lading (maritime), Airway Bill (air) or CMR (road)
Proof of payment / Inward Remittance Certificate (where applicable)
Evidence of non-EU destination (purchase order, import declaration from destination country)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Retrospective adjustment is possible within the general legal limitation period of 5 years (10 years in case of suspected fraud). Incorrect zero-rating triggers the reinstatement of VAT at the standard rate plus default interest and administrative fines; criminal penalties for tax evasion may include imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 100,000.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in conjunction with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking supervision and foreign exchange matters; macroprudential policy is delegated within the euro area framework of the European Central Bank (ECB).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a fully liberalised euro-area jurisdiction. There are no exchange control laws, no distinction between resident and non-resident accounts, and no restrictions on current or capital account transactions under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (free movement of capital, Articles 63–66 TFEU) and the Luxembourg 2004 Money-Laundering and Financing of Terrorism Prevention Law (as amended). Profit remittances, dividend distributions, partnership distributions, loan repayments, and liquidation proceeds from an SCSp may be freely transferred in euro or any foreign currency. A SCSp that is transparent for corporate income tax purposes will not trigger withholding tax at the partnership level; banking and settlement fees are the only practical friction. Beneficial ownership declarations may be requested by banks to comply with know-your-customer rules, but will not impede convertibility or remittance. There is no surrender requirement, no central bank approval, no foreign investment screening applicable to the manufacturing of disposable dialysis hemofilters (ISIC 3250), and no capital import/export licensing for the underlying goods.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. All export proceeds from dialysis hemofilter sales may be retained in any currency, converted to euro with the financing bank at freely negotiated market rates, or used directly for offshore trade settlements. The only obligations arise under general tax law: transfer pricing documentation for intra-group cross-border transactions, and the obligation to include export revenues in the commercial accounts of the SCSp for accounting and filing purposes with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) if the SCSp is registered. No specific Export Proceeds Surrender Certificate is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkees / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for daily treasury, EUR settlement, and trade payments
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account for cross-border trade finance
Capital Escrow Account for inbound capital injection and Operational Account with SWIFT corporate e-banking
Operational Account and wealth-liquidity clearing for foreign principals
Operational Account with dedicated trade finance product suite (LC, guarantees)
Operational Account only for private-family driven structures
Operational Account for lower-volume cooperative structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium in Luxembourg — foreign fintech EMIs and payment institutions (including digital banking platforms) with an EU/EEA passport may legally operate in Luxembourg under the revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and the EU EMI Directive. However, the CSSF requires a formal branch or agent notification from the home-state competent authority before cross-border services begin. A fully offshore, non-EEA digital EMI without a Luxembourg licence or EEA-passport should be considered not viable as a principal transactional bank. In practice, tier-1 domestic banks require a physical account for the SCSp, while an EMI can be used as a complementary clearing rail for low-value working-capital payments if s activity is limited to payment initiation or e-money issuance and the EMI has secure client asset safeguarding. Legal constraints include: (i) the EMI must be authorised in its EEA home state and passported into Luxembourg; (ii) the EMI may not grant credit in the form of trade finance without a supplementary lending licence; (iii) the SCSp general partner must maintain oversight of AML/KYC outsourcing; (iv) capital escrow for injections from non-EEA countries should be held with a fully licensed credit institution, not an EMI, to preserve status in downstream bank interviews.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banks may accept fully remote onboarding for low-risk legal entities under CSSF AML/CFT guidance where a reliable electronic identification procedure (video call, digital identity proofing) is used and no face-to-face contact occurs. For an SCSp with ownership by non-resident principals, the practical mandate of tier-1 banks is to require one of the following: (i) the authorised manager (general partner) appears physically at a Luxembourg branch for initial account opening; or (ii) a documented physical meeting with a Luxembourg notary or approved external counsel occurs and that legal officer confirms the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner. Banks with high/medium KYC risk appetite, e.g. Spuerkees and BGL BNP Paribas, generally waive physical appearance only if the SCSp is established through a strictly regulated Luxembourg professional (ELF, an approved PFS – Professional of the Financial Sector, or a CSSF-supervised fund administration). Remote opening is forbidden if the structure includes a trust, bearer shares, an anonymous foundation, or an unexpected relationship to a high-risk jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) or high-asset-value principals with opaque source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO registry extract (RCS), organisational chart, notarised partnership agreement, passport copies, source-of-funds documentation (audited financial statements, bank references, sale or inheritance deeds), and a written business rationale for the Luxembourg SCSp; each principal must complete a statutory declaration of tax residency, a source-of-wealth questionnaire, and a politically exposed person (PEP) disclosure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade involving medical devices and settlement to high-risk or sanctioned counties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid ISO 13485 certificate, EU CE mark certificate for the disposable dialysis hemofilter, the full supply-chain contract with counterparty information, invoice and bill-of-lading pack, export/import licences or exemption certificates, and a signed attestation that the counterparty is not subject to EU, UN, US, or Luxembourg sanctions; banks will scan counterparties against the Luxembourg SDN list and the CSSF consolidated list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Partnership structure (SCSp) has no minimum capital and may be viewed as a shell vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance dossier containing: the registered office lease contract in Luxembourg, evidence of a local corporate secretary or qualified ELF, anticipated manufacturing or procurement activity related to actual order commitments, cash-flow projection showing real inventory and trade receivables, tax filings or preliminary accounting ledgers, and minutes appointing the national authorised manager. The general partner must be either a Luxembourg resident or an eligible professional.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Significant cash-flows from multiple non-EEA counterparties in a regulated medical sector
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full purchase orders, sea/air waybills, customs declarations, quality certificates per shipment, third-party inspection certificates, insurance policies, and an independent auditor annual confirmation of the accounts of the SCSp; banks may require a cash-flow provenance matrix showing all inbound and outbound counterparties and their connection to dialysis OEM/private-label production.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultra large inbound capital injection above the bank's due-diligence reporting threshold
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Structured capital contribution plan and source-of-funds file: share/purchase deposit agreements, target acquisition documents, loan agreements with bank-acceptable lenders, foreign exchange conversion reports, and an explanation of the commercial synergies; the bank will require the general partner to confirm that the capital is not derived from proceeds of crime and to provide a chart of onward movement to operational account(s).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing should be structured as (i) a capital contribution from the limited partner to the SCSp capital escrow account held at a tier-1 Luxembourg bank; wire instructions must carry SWIFT tag 50K (ordering customer) and tag 59 (beneficiary account), with a purpose code reflecting 'limited partnership capital contribution' in the remittance information (e.g. EU BOP code BKSF or general investment under CSSF statistical requirements); (ii) for any transfer exceeding EUR 10,000, the receiving bank requires the UBO and source-of-funds declaration prepared by the ELF/sponsor. If capital is injected in USD or another non-EUR currency, the correspondent bank must be notified of the final euro conversion; BCL reporting obligations under the Balance of Payments (BOP) framework oblige the bank to identify the transfer as a direct or portfolio investment transaction. For SCSp, the cash injection should not be routed through a personal or unrelated intermediary account, as this triggers enhanced due diligence and delays. The optimal rail is a same-day or target-2 settlement to the Luxembourg bank's nostro account, using the SCSp's IBAN, followed by confirmation to the commercial register RCS if the contribution changes registered capital or share premium.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements for disposable dialysis hemofilter exports, the standard rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103/MT202 single direct transfer for open-account payments to foreign suppliers of polyethersulfone (PESU), hollow-fibre spinning machines, potting adhesives, and shipping services; each MT103 must contain the required purpose code matching Luxembourg BOP classification (e.g. 'medical supply purchase' or 'raw material import') and should bill through an electronic banking B2B interface; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) opened by the Luxembourg bank on behalf of the SCSp in favour of the supplier, governed by UCP 600, with documents drafted to match the SCSp's trade invoices; (3) standby LC or guarantees for OEM distributors when the SCSp supplies private-label products to hospitals; all settlement to non-EU countries should be made by telegraphic transfer (TT/Wire) through the bank's risk-controlled correspondent network, ensuring that the beneficiary bank is not on the corresponding sanctions list. For all outbound transactions above EUR 10,000, the bank's AML transaction-monitoring rail will flag the Bonafide transaction; the SCSp should maintain a central digital proof database with invoice, customs entry, goods receipt note, and transport history for KYC/sanction reviews. The entity should never split trade payments into multiple sub-threshold transfers to avoid audit triggers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla foreign exchange forwards (contract-negotiated EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/JPY) with a registered Luxembourg credit institution or an eligible EEA FX counterparty; no physical delivery of capital is required for the SCSp if the hedging contract is explicitly linked to a transactional commercial exposure, such as purchase of PESU resin or a confirmed export invoice.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are permissible when trading certain restricted or non-convertible currencies (e.g. emerging-market currencies) as long as the SCSp contractually settles the differential in EUR via a CSTO-compliant bank; NDFs must be booked as derivatives and marked-to-market in the SCSp's accounting records; no NDF may be used as a disguised speculative position without underlying export/procurement exposure.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR vs USD or EUR vs CNY) are permissible for matching long-term liquidity mismatches, such as financing a foreign production prepayment while receiving export proceeds in hard currency; the swap must be collateralised under the Credit Support Annex (CSA) and approved by the SCSp's treasury risk policy.

Commodity and freight hedging in the form of futures on polymer prices or Baltic Exchange freight indices, if cleared through a recognised clearing house (e.g. Eurex, LCH), may be used to stabilise the input cost of the dialysis hemofilter supply chain, but such instruments are ancillary and must be separately authorised by the Luxembourg bank's credit approval documentation.
Interest rate swaps or caps on EURIBOR-linked financing lines may be used solely to hedge the interest-rate risk of the working-capital facility supporting the manufacturing cycle.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO register confirmation (article 16, law of 13 January 2019)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE) – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 March each calendar year; modifications resulting from shareholding transfers must be filed within one month of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EUR 500–1,250 per offence; repeated or aggravated non-compliance up to EUR 50,000; potential criminal liability for directors/managers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) of the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the SCSp's financial year-end (for 31 December fiscal year-end: 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCSL formal notice after two months of default; administrative fine up to EUR 25,000; persistent default triggers administrative strike-off and judicial dissolution; directors/managers jointly liable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return – pass-through information return for the transparent partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the following calendar year for a 31 December tax year; extended to 31 December when e-filed through an approved tax advisor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 0.6% of net tax due per commenced month of delay (max 12%, minimum EUR 50); late-payment interest at 4% per annum; tax assessment by default (taxation d'office).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent annual audit (by an approved statutory auditor, réviseur d'entreprises agréé) if the SCSp exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: total balance sheet > EUR 6.0 million; net turnover > EUR 12.0 million; average headcount > 50. Also mandatory for public-interest entities, AIFs under CSSF supervision, and when the partnership agreement or syndicate contract so requires.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the Law of 19 December 2002 (implementing Directive 2013/34/EU); EU-endorsed IFRS permitted for consolidated accounts; the SCSp is tax-transparent for corporate income tax and net wealth tax purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: All limited and general partner shareholding data must be confirmed in the RBE annually by 15 March. Any ownership transfer during the year must be declared to the RBE within one month of the transfer being recorded in the register of partners; the SCSp must also update its statutory register of partners at the registered office and make it available for inspection without charge.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of partners (limited and general partners, series of shares if applicable)
Register of decisions and minutes of partners' meetings and written resolutions
Register of managers and general partner's directors (identification details)
Accounting books, accountability ledger, and correspondence files

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 1,200 – EUR 4,500 (USD 1,300 – USD 4,900) depending on registered office provider and frequency of filing assistance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 8,000 – EUR 25,000 (USD 8,700 – USD 27,000) for a mid-size manufacturing partnership; lower for micro-entities exempt from audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is tax-transparent; no CIT at entity level. Partners taxed individually. IP box regime may apply to qualifying income (80% exemption).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via MyGuichet.lu electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after fiscal year-end (extensions possible up to 12 months)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg tax representative details if applicable
Non-resident partners must report their share in their home jurisdiction; Luxembourg return is informational

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and exemptions (e.g., IP box, investment allowances)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only applicable to Luxembourg-resident partners; non-residents claim via treaty
Non-resident partners may claim foreign tax credits in their residence country

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of EUR 100 per day, up to EUR 10,000; plus interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form 500 (or 501) to Luxembourg tax authority along with a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the partner's jurisdiction; treaty relief may reduce WHT to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or applicable DTA
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 10%, treaty-reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive; Interest: statutory 15%, treaty-reduced to 0% under EU Directive

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50 million group revenue for Master File; EUR 1 million intercompany transactions for Local File
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: ESR applies to Luxembourg entities engaged in specific activities; manufacturing requires physical presence, qualified employees, and operational expenditure in Luxembourg

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income or overstating deductions to reduce tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EUR 250,000 or 2x the evaded tax; criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Lack of economic substance (no physical office, no employees, no real business activity) while claiming tax benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax treaty benefits, retroactive tax assessments, penalties up to EUR 100,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes and subject to director disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML procedures, suspicious transaction reporting, or beneficial ownership disclosure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1 million; criminal penalties for money laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability, imprisonment up to 5 years, and asset seizure
